newsitem.title: UK: European bourses climb, boosted by Wall St. [CORRECTED 13:00 GMT]
newsitem.headline: European bourses climb, boosted by Wall St. [CORRECTED 13:00 GMT]

text.p: European bourses rose sharply on Tuesday, building on Monday's recovery and fired by an overnight surge on Wall Street that wiped out "grey Friday's" heavy losses.

The dollar got off to a firm start against the mark and yen, buoyed by the New York stock market's recovery after turmoil sparked by Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan who questioned the "irrational exuberance" of the markets.
The strongest performer was Frankfurt, which shot up 1.23 percent in early floor trading as investors cheered Wall Street's rally and stronger dollar. The Dow finished some 82 points up on Monday.
"The market factors are all there," said one dealer, "I think we are back on track."
The DAX index was reached 2,892.45 points at one point, again approaching the 2,914.61 record it achieved only a day before global market jitters last Friday forced it down four percent.

Many dealers are hoping for a resumption of the traditional pre-Christmas rally on the stock market, and believe that if the DAX can regain the 2,900 point level it will trigger fresh buying interest.
"If we hit 2,900, then we will be chasing 3,000," another dealer said.

Early advancers included carmaker Volkswagen AG, up after its chief executive Ferdinand Piech appeared to take a more conciliatory note in the company's feud with General Motors, by expressing his regret over the cost and trouble caused.

Europe's robust performance came after rallies in Asian stock markets where investors, in the second straight day of share-price gains, read the Dow's rise as a sign that U.S. markets had shrugged off Greenspan's negative comments.

In London, the FTSE index rose 0.35 percent (corrects from 35 percent) with investors stunned by the rapid turnaround in sentiment. At one point on Friday, slumping shares wiped 25 billion pounds ($41 billion) off the market's value.
Traders said the market was underpinned by a resilient appetite for stocks: "There's too much cash around for markets to go down that far," said one, referring to Friday's tumble.
Yet some traders remained uneasy about the seemingly unstoppable advance in the U.S. The Dow has risen around 28 percent since its year low in January.

"It is slightly worrying that people seem to be ignoring what Greenspan said," one trader said. "He may well decide to go a step further and put rates up as he must be worried that the growth in asset prices in the U.S. could fuel inflation."
In Paris, French stocks rose more 0.4 percent, extending their rebound after Friday's fright and with traders expecting the market to resume its advance.
On currency markets, the dollar was firmer in early trade, helped by Wall Street and Swiss franc losses following confirmation of a weak Swiss economy in the third quarter.
The Swiss franc eyed 1996 lows at 1.3330 per dollar and set fresh 30-month lows against the mark.

Swiss gross domestic product dropped an annualised 0.7 percent in the third quarter, while the Swiss Commission for Economic Policy forecast growth of just 0.5 percent for all of 1997. The figures underlined recent statements from the Swiss National Bank that monetary policy will remain loose, keeping the Swiss franc under pressure, analysts said.

"The dollar has made a solid bounce back from last week, having blown some of the froth off the markets on Friday, and many of the prior themes will now resume, especially the weak mark and Swiss franc trends," said Tony Norfield, treasury economist at ABN Amro.
The dollar was at 1.5568 marks and 113.45 in early trading, up on the levels seen in late Europe on Monday. The currency slipped slightly later against the mark.
CURRENCIES AT 1015 GMT
The dollar was quoted at 113.35 yen and 1.5545 marks against 113.26 yen and 1.5556 marks in late Europe on Monday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1015 GMT
The FTSE 100 index of leading British shares were 16.3 points higher at 4,027.9
In Paris, the CAC-40 share index was up 9.51 at 2,265.35.
The 30-share DAX index in Frankfurt was up 25.29 at 2,882.53
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold opened easier at weaker at $368.15 an ounce, compared to Monday's close of $368.95. Silver was at $4.78, down one cent.
